selected_result: Theorem 3.4: probabilistic componentwise backward and forward errors for matrix multiplication

bibliographic_source.title: A New Approach to Probabilistic Rounding Error Analysis

paper_locations.anchor: Theorem 3.4 and equations (3.11)-(3.12); printed column-index mismatch requires resolution

task_clarification: For A in R^(m x n), B in R^(n x p), and C=A*B, compute CHat in floating-point arithmetic under the source Model 2.1.

The theorem states a per-column backward representation cHat_j=(A+DeltaA_j)*b_j with |DeltaA_j|<=gammaTilde_n(lambda)*|A| and probability at least Q(lambda,m*n), and a full matrix bound |CHat-C|<=gammaTilde_n(lambda)*|A|*|B| with probability at least Q(lambda,m*n*p).
The paper prints j=1:n in equation (3.11) although B has p columns and the proof combines p column instances. This packet is not admitted until that source conflict is resolved explicitly.
scope_constraints: Keep the source's Model 2.1, all rectangular dimensions, componentwise inequalities, and exact Q and gammaTilde factors.
Do not quietly replace the printed j-domain, drop equation (3.11), or treat this draft as an authorized correction.
Do not assume the backward perturbations or forward-error event in the execution model.
